title: A decision without discussion
topic: Equality and fair treatment of patients
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on an elderly care ward. Mr Dean, 61, has a learning disability and has been admitted with a chest infection. He is improving.

On the ward round, the registrar asks you to complete a DNACPR form "because of his learning disability". No one has discussed it with Mr Dean or his sister, who visits daily.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.detailed: Completing the form on this basis would be wrong and could harm him.

options.text: Record your disagreement in the medical notes, then complete the form.
options.detailed: Documenting your concern doesn't stop the harm.

options.text: Tell his sister the registrar is discriminating against him.
options.brief: Undermines the team before the issue is raised.
options.detailed: His sister should be involved, but raising it with the registrar first is fairer and more effective.

options.text: Report the registrar to the Care Quality Commission.
options.detailed: This should be addressed directly and through local routes first.

options.text: Leave the form for the night team to decide.
options.detailed: The problem would still need addressing.

options.text: Point out that a learning disability isn't grounds for DNACPR.
options.brief: DNACPR decisions must be based on clinical factors, not disability.
options.detailed: Making a resuscitation decision because of someone's learning disability is discriminatory. Raising this politely gives the registrar a chance to reconsider.

options.text: Involve Mr Dean and his sister in any discussion.
options.brief: He, and those close to him, should be involved.
options.detailed: Decisions about resuscitation should be discussed with the patient where possible, with reasonable adjustments, and with those close to him.

options.text: Ask the learning disability liaison nurse for support.
options.detailed: The liaison nurse can help adapt communication and make sure his needs are understood.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you challenge a discriminatory resuscitation decision and make sure the patient is involved.
explanation.keyDetails: The reason given is his learning disability. He is improving. No discussion has taken place. His sister visits daily.
explanation.reasoning: [F] challenges the reasoning, [G] involves him and his sister, and [H] brings in specialist support. The distractors comply ([A], [B]), undermine the team ([C]), escalate disproportionately ([D]), or avoid it ([E]).
explanation.competing: [B] might seem a compromise, but the decision itself is the problem.

references.title: Treatment and care towards the end of life: good practice in decision making
references.note: Decisions about CPR must not be based on disability.
